title: Ambiguous marbles
statement: A bag holds $3$ red and $5$ blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn. What is the probability that they are the same colour? Give your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
hints: Add the all-red and the all-blue pairs.
solution: There are $\binom82 = 28$ pairs of marbles, of which $\binom32 + \binom52 = 3 + 10 = 13$ are the same colour, so the probability is $\tfrac{13}{28}$. Why this works. favorable-over-total: the probability is a ratio of two pair counts.
check_program:
from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import combinations
b = 'RRRBBBBB'
p = list(combinations(range(8), 2))
print(Fraction(sum(1 for i, j in p if b[i] == b[j]), len(p)))
